arguments.value: Two Ghanaian patients presented with new-onset seizures and no major past medical history, both with epidemiologic risk factors for Taenia solium exposure (rural residence, free-ranging pigs, pork consumption). Neuroimaging showed parenchymal brain cysts with eccentric scolex consistent with neurocysticercosis; one patient had vesicular-stage lesions in the frontal lobes and insular cortex, and the other had vesicular plus calcified lesions in the frontal and parietal lobes. Both had normal labs, no focal neurologic deficits, were treated with anti-seizure medication plus albendazole and corticosteroids, and had no seizure recurrence on follow-up.
